d.details: The Strike was built for a Coordinator. Every sortie leaves Autumn with bruises from G-forces a Coordinator frame would absorb, hand tremors, migraines he hides from medical. Mu notices combat reactions that don't track. Autumn avoids post-combat data reviews. The crew's gratitude masks their willingness to let him destroy himself — and he sees the dynamic clearly. The ticking clock: cumulative physical damage will eventually degrade his piloting below combat viability, and the Manifold Resonance he won't name is leaving data anomalies someone will eventually examine.
d.cost: Every sortie costs physical capacity he cannot regenerate. Discovery of Manifold Resonance costs his personhood in a world that dissects the biologically different. Hiding it costs accuracy in self-assessment. The intersection: when the physical damage is bad enough that only Resonance keeps him competitive, the secret becomes visible in the gap between what his body can do and what the combat logs show.

Kira Yamato defected to ZAFT. Everyone aboard knows. Lacus Clyne does not. Every interaction she has is shaped by a betrayal she's unaware of — the crew's hostility reads as ideology to her when it's actually grief. Her political lens interprets anti-Coordinator sentiment as factional when it's personal. When she learns the truth, every read she's built recalibrates. If command tells her, it's framed as briefing rather than confession. If she discovers it herself — overheard, pieced together — she learns that everyone chose to keep it from her.

Lacus's misreads accumulate with every interaction built on missing context. The crew's hostility intensifies because she doesn't understand its source and therefore can't navigate it. Autumn carries the weight of knowing the name she hasn't heard. Whoever finally speaks it pays the price of being the one who broke the silence.
